clue.text: Humanitarian outfit embarrassed and annoyed

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
annoyed means cross

explanation.surface: An aid agency that is both ashamed and irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international humanitarian relief organisation, an outfit in the sense of an organisation.

clue.text: Character willing to bring old maid, perhaps

parts.note: a card is a character, an eccentric person
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to bring along an elderly spinster.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Maid is a children's card game in which players avoid being left holding the odd queen; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a well-known example of a game played with a pack of cards.

clue.text: Greet workers led by wag

indicators.note: in an across clue, the workers come after the wag, so the wag's word leads

parts.note: to wag is to shake to and fro
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Welcoming labourers who follow a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wag' looks like a joker leading the workers, but here it is the verb, to shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and pumping someone's hand is a customary way of greeting them.

clue.text: Odds studied in advance

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Betting prices pored over beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, short for starting price, is a British horse-racing term for the odds on offer as a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread is to extend or progress outward, as a fire or rumour advances across an area.

clue.text: Relative in Africa, untraceable

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters spanning the words Africa and untraceable

explanation.surface: A family member somewhere in Africa who cannot be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family relation, a relative.

clue.text: Look on ship for a kind of cosmetic

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: an eye is a look, as in 'cast an eye over'
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Glancing at a vessel in search of make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn along the edge of the eyelids, one type of cosmetic.

clue.text: A launch, aimlessly drifting

parts.note: to float a company is to launch it on the stock market

explanation.surface: A small boat set loose and wandering on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' suggests a motor boat, but it is the verb, to float.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting without direction on water is buoyant and floating, not sunk.

clue.text: Record American sports event

parts.note: a record is a disc of recorded music

explanation.surface: A US athletics fixture that set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus throw is a field event in athletics, a sporting event.

clue.text: Leave suddenly, half of Deal affected

indicators.note: the first two of the four letters in Deal are taken

parts.note: camp means affected, theatrically exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: Someone quits the Kentish town of Deal abruptly, with half the town touched.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart abruptly or secretly, to leave suddenly.

clue.text: To provoke second son is unnecessary

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or goad them

explanation.surface: Annoying a younger child is gratuitous.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless is a synonym of unnecessary, something not required.

clue.text: Dictates changes in what may prove conclusive

indicators.note: a word that alters, telling us to rearrange the letters of Dictates

explanation.surface: Orders are altered in a decisive trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a decisive trial that settles whether something is genuine, so it proves conclusive.

clue.text: One famous singer, not old — he died escaping Crete

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word 'not' asks for the old letter to be left out of the singer's name

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor

explanation.surface: A celebrated tenor who died while fleeing a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek myth: the boy who escaped Crete on wings of wax and feathers flew too near the sun and fell to his death.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the son of Daedalus fled imprisonment in Crete on artificial wings and drowned when the wax melted.

clue.text: At times fashionable, with that being so

parts.note: now means fashionable, up to date
and means with, joining things
then means in that case, that being so

explanation.surface: Occasionally trendy, given that.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Poet in centre of Corfu

parts.note: home means in, as in 'is he home?'

indicators.note: the middle of the five letters of Corfu is picked

explanation.surface: A bard visiting the middle of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the poet on Corfu, but it gives HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey is the archetypal epic poet.

clue.text: Gain an advantage over rotten marshal at once

indicators.note: rotten means bad or spoiled, so the letters of marshal at once are reworked

explanation.surface: Outdoing a bad marshal immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to get ahead of rivals by acting first, gaining an advantage over them.

clue.text: A golf rep playing a game

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of a golf rep are moving about in play

explanation.surface: A golfing sales representative out on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which players vault over each other's bent backs.

clue.text: Figure blocking female in lift

indicators.note: a figure blocking the female sits inside her, obstructing the way through

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
eight is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A shape obstructing a woman inside an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' suggests a British elevator, but it is the verb, to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to raise or increase, which is what lifting something does.

clue.text: Involved person admitting Home Office failures

indicators.note: the jumbled word lets the Home Office in, taking it inside
involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters of person are jumbled

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for the Home Office, the UK government department

explanation.surface: Someone implicated, let into a government department, proves a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' rearranges the letters of the word person to make NOPERS; 'admitting' then lets the government department's initials in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no chance of success is a hopeless case, a failure.

clue.text: Gallop in pursuit

definitions.meaning: to rush along at full speed
a ... is one's chosen occupation, a calling followed through life

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for rushing headlong and a noun for one's working life or vocation.

clue.text: Cambridge college student's last Bordeaux

parts.note: Clare College is one of the colleges of Cambridge University

indicators.note: the final letter of student's is taken

explanation.surface: An undergraduate's last bottle of French red at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'student's last' gives T, not the student's last drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Look about in box in carriage

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in 'an air of confidence'

indicators.note: the word about is placed inside the word for box

parts.note: to box is to fight
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Glancing around inside a crate in a railway coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' means conveyance of goods here, not a railway coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the transporting of goods, and freight carried by aircraft is one form of it.

clue.text: Stupidly trail round district of Venice

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters of trail are arranged foolishly, out of order

parts.note: O is a round shape

explanation.surface: Foolishly following a path around part of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a walker on a path; 'Stupidly' rearranges the path word to make RIALT, and 'round' supplies a circle-shaped letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the commercial quarter of Venice around its famous bridge.

clue.text: Telephone everyone in competition

indicators.note: everyone is placed inside the word for competition

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Ringing all the entrants in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up is to ring someone on the phone.

clue.text: Sat, agitated, with phone going off in carriage

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of Sat are shaken about
going off means exploding or going wrong, so the letters of phone are scrambled too

explanation.surface: Someone sat nervously in a coach while a mobile rang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' gives STA from SAT, and 'going off' gives NHOPE from PHONE; the two scrambles sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage with one seat, named after its designer.

clue.text: Knocks over box

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for knocks is read bottom to top

parts.note: raps are knocks

explanation.surface: Blows send a crate tumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is the verb, to fight with fists, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Couple in conversation decline sweet

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so the word for couple is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a pair is a couple
a drop is a decline or fall

explanation.surface: Two people falling out while talking about candy.
explanation.walkthrough: A pear drop is a British boiled sweet, pear-shaped and pear-flavoured.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear drop is a hard boiled confection, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Ambassador taken in by right-wing supposition

indicators.note: the ambassador is enclosed by the right-winger, taken inside

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right
HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy duped by a conservative politician makes a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests deceived, but here it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a hypothesis or conjecture, a supposition.

clue.text: See actress in great cocktail dress before start of Oscars

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of great are mixed

parts.note: garb is dress, clothing

indicators.note: the first letter of Oscars is taken

explanation.surface: Spot a film star in a fine cocktail dress at the Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail dress' reads as a garment; 'cocktail' rearranges GREAT and 'dress' is GARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.
